speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe the rash on your trunk and extremities in more detail, such as whether it is red, raised, or blistering? Also, does the rash seem to follow a specific pattern, like spreading from your trunk outward?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the rash on her trunk feel sandpaper-like to the touch, and is there a "strawberry" appearance to her tongue? Also, has she had any recent exposure to someone with a sore throat or a known case of Scarlet Fever?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the facial rash you mentioned have a "slapped cheek" appearance, and did the body rash begin on your trunk and spread to your extremities a few days after the facial rash appeared? I also need to check if you have any swollen lymph nodes or joint pain.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: Attends local school. Lives with parents and one younger sibling. No recent travel history.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on the "slapped cheek" appearance and the subsequent body rash, I am fairly confident this is Erythema Infectiosum, also known as Fifth Disease. To confirm the diagnosis and rule out other causes, I will request specific blood work. REQUEST TEST: Parvovirus B19 IgM and IgG antibodies.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Parvovirus B19 IgM and IgG antibody tests were not included in the provided data; only Complete Blood Count (WBC: Normal, Hemoglobin: Normal, Platelets: Slightly elevated), Throat Culture (Negative for Group A Streptococcus), Vital Signs, and Skin Examination findings are available.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the negative throat culture and the classic "slapped cheek" rash followed by a reticular body rash, the clinical picture strongly supports Fifth Disease despite the unavailable viral serology. I will now proceed with my final assessment based on these findings. DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease).
